task.summary: Default task
save fx states and protect framebuffer copy by disabling all interrupts
save fx states and protect framebuffer copy by disabling all interrupts
enhance scheduler to support yield and preempt

Enable both APIC and PIT timer. Use APIC for process scheduling and PIT for clock/time keeping. Implement yield() for various wait scenarios. Add a schedule_runner_process that will ensure that the timer interrupt based scheduler has at-least one process to execute and return from timer irq - so, other interrupts like PIT timer interrupt will get a chance to trigger and allow sleeping processes to wake up. Basically, this will avoid the main process scheduling loop inside the timer interrupt handler from getting into an infinite loop of processes that are not ready to run.

align stack for loaded user-process to 16 byte to ensure SSE/SSE2/SSE3 instructions don't cause General Protection Fault

Remove the error-code (if any) from stack in interrupt/exception handler upfront before saving the registers to ensure rsp is 16 byte aligned. without error-code, the stack has 5 params * 8 byte = 40 bytes. Save registers will push 120 bytes for registers and 512 bytes for xxm registers - total 512 + 120 + 40 = 672 -> 16 byte aligned. Adding error-code will make rsp 680 bytes which is not 16 byte aligned, which makes fxsave fail with General Protection Fault

separate stack frame for timer vs page-fault vs rest. It is paricurlarly important to keep stack separate for time vs page-fault because page-fault handler yields by calling timer interrupt (int 0x20) and hence they can't both use same stack frame. This is achieved using different IST values in IDT definition of these interrupts

MESSAGE.value: added KLog utility. Introduced a new kernel mode called KERNEL_ROOT to be used while initializing syslog that ensures there is no race condition with setting KERNEL_MODE during timer interrupt

kernel should be compiled with -mno-red-zone compiler flag to ensure the compiler doesn't access the red-zone stack area while executing interrupt code because they use run time stack switch from ring3 to ring0 and there is no reserved red-zone in this case
set ist flag to 0 for regular interrupts - so they use RSP0 when switching from ring3 to ring0 and continue to use existing RSP when not switching rings
a util method added to IrqManager to check if an interrupt is enabled
if interrupt is disabled (i.e. cli) then do a tight loop for 100000 times in poll wait - this is possibly happening because the poll wait is being called from inside an interrupt handler

Revert the logic to use IST specific stack frame instead of RSP0 - this will ensure that all interrupts whether they trigger ring3->ring0 switch, will use an interrupt stack that is 16 byte aligned and each process/thread will have its own stack space mapped to the same IST stack top - so, interrupts that trigger across process switch are using different stack space without overwriting each other's stack.
E1000 NIC interrupt handler is decoupled from main processing by writing the event to an async queue
Fixed bug in WAIT_INT logic to wait until the event queue is non-empty

special handling for schedule runner (.sr) to ensure it runs on every invocation irrespective of whether the sleep interval has elapsed - this is required because in case an interrupt occurs while executing .sr and if the interrupt calls sleep with a non-zero interval then we could end-up with all processes on the scheduler in wait or sleep mode and the timer interrupt will be in a loop to find the next ready process. If all processes are in sleep mode then they will not be picked up because PIT will not fire while timer interrupt is active
